definition: In this context, an experimental method is a research approach used to test whether a counselling program has an effect by giving it to one group and comparing their results with a control group and with their own scores before and after the program. The packet specifically describes this as a quasi-experimental method.

reasons: The packet describes the study as using a quasi-experimental method, not an experimental method, so the requested sense is not supported.

The definition adds a specific pretest-posttest control-group description as if it were the term’s meaning; the packet only supports this as one study design, not a general definition of “experimental method.”

The packet does not define the term “experimental method”; it only states that the study used a “quasi-experimental method,” so the definition’s identification of “experimental method” as the approach is not supported by the packet.

The definition says the method is “used to test whether a counselling program has an effect” by comparing groups and pre/post; while the packet describes a quasi-experimental study with control vs experimental groups and pre/post measurement, it does not support labeling that approach specifically as an “experimental method” (vs “quasi-experimental”).
